result.summary:
DIAGNOSIS ISS-0926 (Q-926/GH-2106) -- CONFIRMED. Correction to the issue text: body_template IS sent, but as the RAW UNRENDERED template; {{variables.X}} placeholders go out literally.

0.5 REGISTRY: no recurrence. Related resolved entries: ISS-0917 (catalog pinned dispatch), ISS-0930 (seed endpoints), ISS-0932 (21-day timer path; filed this issue), ISS-0950. None fixed body rendering. REQ-215 design (lib/letflow/design/req215-service-task-engine-wiring.md:1063-1070, Open Question 2) and q915-regulatory-review-21day-timer-path.md s4 (lines 127-150) both explicitly deferred it. Known deferred gap, not a regression.

ROOT CAUSE (reproduced by running ServiceTask.parse_config_from_node_attributes on the real fixture node via mix run --no-start with a throwaway random master key; DB-backed tests could NOT be run -- Postgres unreachable, ecto.migrate fails):
 - Parse: lib/letflow/engine/service_task.ex:226 `body_template: Map.get(attrs, "body_template")` verbatim (reproduced: {"reason":"{{variables.reason}}"} parses unchanged). URL comes from attribute "endpoint" (service_task.ex:205), NOT "url_template"; so the fixture's "endpoint" attrs are valid (reproduced: {:ok, %Config{route_kind: :inline_url, url_template: ".../regulatory-notice", body_template: nil}}).
 - Store: lib/letflow/engine.ex:1117 config_snapshot_map stores "body_template" => config.body_template (raw) beside "rendered_url" (:1121). Built at activation in finish_service_task_arm_attrs (engine.ex:1068-1092) called from resolve_service_task_arm_attrs (engine.ex:967-995), the only place `variables` are in scope. The URL is rendered there (:973 inline, :983 catalog) and frozen. No rendered_body is ever computed.
 - Dispatch: lib/letflow/engine/service_task_dispatcher.ex:719 (inline) and :741 (catalog): `rendered_body = row.config_snapshot["body_template"]` -> http_transport/3 (:304) -> do_http_transport (:346) -> body_or_empty (:388). So rendered_body is non-nil in production whenever a node has body_template, but it is the raw template, computed never. Content-type application/json is injected iff body_template non-nil (dispatcher :375-386, @http_content_type :100). The dispatcher poller has no access to instance variables, so rendering must happen at activation (like rendered_url, frozen); dispatch-time rendering would break the freeze contract (dispatcher design s5.6 "re-renders nothing, ever").
 - Renderer: engine.ex:1152-1156 render_service_task_url/2, regex ~r/\{\{\s*variables\.([a-zA-Z0-9_]+)\s*\}\}/, flat key only. Stringify (engine.ex:1158-1165): nil->"", binary raw, number/atom to_string, map/list Jason.encode!. NO escaping of any kind. URL safety = UrlValidator.validate on the final URL at dispatch (dispatcher.ex:331; gate :service_task_ssrf_validation_enabled). The comment at engine.ex:1138-1147 says body rendering is out of scope and tells a future requirement to replace the function.
 - Why tests did not catch: test/letflow/scripts/regulatory_review_timer_path_fixture_test.exs T8 (~line 267/184) PINS "no body_template" on regulatory-auto-escalation and mutation M9 (371-376) asserts adding a literal body_template turns T8 red; no test asserts a rendered body. Existing body tests only use nil: service_task_dispatcher_test.exs:88, service_task_wiring_test.exs:625, engine_catalog_service_task_test.exs:307 (key list).

JSON-INJECTION RISK / ESCAPING OPTIONS: raw substitution (what the URL renderer does) into a JSON template lets a value containing a quote, backslash or newline break the body or inject keys (reason = x","admin":true). Variables come from HUMAN_TASK outputs, sub-process outputs and SERVICE_TASK responses, so this is tenant-supplied data. Options:
 A) Per-value JSON-string escaping (Jason.encode! the stringified value, strip outer quotes); placeholders must sit INSIDE a quoted JSON string in the template (documented constraint). Smallest change. Maps/lists become escaped strings. Risk LOW-MEDIUM. RECOMMENDED.
 B) Whole-token typed JSON substitution: bare placeholder `{"reason": {{variables.reason}}}` replaced by Jason.encode!(value) (nil->null, numbers/maps native). Injection-proof by construction, typed values, but a new authoring convention and must handle placeholders inside string literals. Risk MEDIUM.
 C) Decode body_template as JSON, substitute only in string leaves (whole-string placeholder -> typed value), re-encode. Strongest (structure cannot break), fails closed on invalid template JSON. Largest change, new failure mode at activation. Risk MEDIUM-HIGH.
 D) Raw substitution identical to the URL renderer: REJECT (injection).
 Content-type is hardcoded application/json, so non-JSON bodies are unsupported today. Keep INV-2/INV-8: never log/echo rendered body or variables (iss0917 design line ~649). Freeze the result as config_snapshot["rendered_body"]; the dispatcher (719/741) prefers it, falling back to raw body_template only if CODE-DESIGNER decides in-flight old rows must still dispatch. Update the snapshot type in service_task_dispatcher.md:299 and config_snapshot_map @spec. Missing-variable policy ("" like the URL renderer vs typed error) is a design decision.

CATALOG PATH: body_template is a NODE attribute only; the catalog supplies none of method/body_template/headers/retry_limit (iss0917 design line 258). Both route kinds share config_snapshot_map, so one render step in finish_service_task_arm_attrs (variables must be threaded in, or rendered by the two callers at :973/:983) covers both.

DECISION RECORDS (grep -il over docs/migration/decisions): 0022, 0027, 0029, 0030 mention SERVICE_TASK/SSRF but NONE settles body rendering semantics (0027 = catalog install policy / SSRF stub asymmetry). Only design docs touch it (req215 OQ2, service_task.md:421 "rendering is out of scope", q915 s4), all deferrals. No decision-record conflict; the escaping choice should be recorded as a new design decision with REVIEWER sign-off.

FIXTURE / EO-002: node regulatory-auto-escalation (test/fixtures/qa/meridian_regulatory_compliance_review_process_definition.json, version 1.2) = SERVICE_TASK, endpoint https://httpbin.org/anything/compliance/regulatory-notice, POST, timeout_ms 300000, no body_template. Inbound: timeout-risk-evaluation (21-day timer on risk-evaluation, the single non-conditioned edge) and e10 (post-remediation-check, remediation_status=='unresolved'). Outbound e5 -> end-closed. Scenario EO-002 (regulatory-compliance-review-bafin.yaml:105-121) requires audit_event for POST /compliance/regulatory-notice "with payload containing reason 'sla_breach_30_days'" for sim-meridian-review-001.
 Node types (graph.ex:146-154, 298-307): START END HUMAN_TASK SERVICE_TASK EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY PARALLEL_GATEWAY TIMER SUB_PROCESS. There is NO script/assign/set-variable node. Variables are set only by HUMAN_TASK outputs, SUB_PROCESS outputs and SERVICE_TASK decoded response bodies (VariableMerge, engine.ex ~3179). The timer path sets NO variable; remediation_status exists only on the e10 route (absent -> renders "" on the timer route). So no variable is present on both inbound paths that distinguishes them.
 Fixture-only options (no lib change; feasible today because the raw body_template IS sent verbatim):
  F1) SPLIT the node: regulatory-auto-escalation (timer inbound, literal body_template {"reason":"sla_breach_30_days"}, e5 -> end-closed) plus a new node for e10 (literal {"reason":"remediation_unresolved"}, -> end-closed). Distinguishes paths exactly; literal bodies need no rendering or escaping. Needs fixture version bump 1.2 -> 1.3 (seed script only replaces an ACTIVE definition when strictly newer). Risk LOW.
  F2) One node with static reason: WRONG on e10. Reject.
  F3) Pre-escalation SERVICE_TASK per inbound edge whose JSON response sets variables.reason: needs an endpoint returning a controlled body (httpbin /anything echoes the request; circular), adds external calls. Not recommended.
  F4) Conditional edges on a variable: no timer-path variable exists and the timer edge is deliberately non-conditioned (fixture description, T5). Infeasible.
 Engine option E1) body rendering alone does NOT fix EO-002, since it still needs a path-distinguishing value; it adds value combined with F1 (e.g. body {"review_id":"{{variables.review_id}}","reason":"sla_breach_30_days"}).
 CAVEAT: EO-002's verification method is audit_event, but the engine never records the outbound body in audit/logs (iss0917 design forbids it). A payload check on an audit event may be unsatisfiable regardless of rendering. CODE-DESIGNER / BA should confirm what EO-002 actually reads (httpbin echo, or dispatch row config_snapshot where a frozen "rendered_body" would make it assertable).

RECOMMENDATION (ranked by risk): (1) F1 fixture split with literal reasons, version 1.3: smallest, no lib change, resolves the timer-path reason and the e10 correctness concern. (2) F1 plus lib change: render body_template at activation with option A and freeze config_snapshot["rendered_body"], the real fix for the issue title (lets the notice carry review_id etc.). lib change needed: yes (MINOR), owner ELIXIR-DEV. It IS on a tenant-data path (instance variables flow into an outbound HTTP body; injection; INV-2/INV-8), so SECURITY-REVIEWER gate applies.

AFFECTED FILES: lib/letflow/engine.ex (renderer 1148-1165, config_snapshot_map 1111-1122, finish_service_task_arm_attrs 1068-1092, callers 967-995); lib/letflow/engine/service_task_dispatcher.ex (719, 741, config_from_snapshot ~800); design docs lib/letflow/design/service_task.md:421 and service_task_dispatcher.md:299 (+ new design). Fixture: test/fixtures/qa/meridian_regulatory_compliance_review_process_definition.json. Tests: test/letflow/scripts/regulatory_review_timer_path_fixture_test.exs (T1 :119/:239 version, T8 :267 body pin, M9 :371, T9 :271), test/letflow/engine/regulatory_review_timer_path_test.exs (:66 version, :156-180 node ids), test/letflow/engine/service_task_wiring_test.exs:625, test/letflow/engine/service_task_dispatcher_test.exs:88 (plus new render/injection tests), test/letflow/engine_catalog_service_task_test.exs:307 (@inline_keys if a rendered_body key is added), test/specs/ISS-0932.md. If fixture version/shape changes: test/fixtures/simulation/meridian/process_policy_binding.yaml (nodes :33, edges :92-113; its own version field is "1.0", separate), test/fixtures/uat/process-definition-aliases/proc-meridian-regulatory-compliance-review.yaml, test/scripts/persona_actor_seed_drift_test.exs (:20), scripts/seed_meridian_definition.sh:6 header "v1.2", design docs q915-regulatory-review-21day-timer-path.md and iss0930-seed-service-task-endpoints.md, docs/issues/ISS-0926.yaml (correct the description: body is sent raw, not omitted), scenario EO-002 text.
LIMITS: DB-backed tests could not run (Postgres unreachable); diagnosis = code reading plus a pure parse reproduction. No file other than this handoff was modified.
